name: Dev-via-spec Challenger Accept → Architect Handoff
description: When the dev-via-spec-challenger emits decide(action=accept), the adversarial gate has passed and the plan is committed. This rule fires on that signal and spawns the dev-via-spec-architect for the curation pass — extracting the chain consensus from the challenger's accept reason, structuring it via emit_dev_via_spec_artifact (R3.4b), which renders a human-readable markdown spec to docs/specs/ and mints marker triples on the calling loop. The architect's decide(seed_requirements_emitted) is terminal — no further rule fires. ADR-031 §addendum 2026-05-02.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.dev-via-spec-architect
on_enter.prompt: The dev-via-spec challenger accepted the plan. Challenger loop id: $entity.instance (passed as prior_loop_id in your task properties). Call read_loop_result with that loop id to read the challenger's verdict; the chain context is summarised in the verdict's reason field. Extract the chain's substance (goal, context, actors, integration_points, seed_requirements as epic-shaped scope items, provenance loop_ids) and call emit_dev_via_spec_artifact with structured args per your `10-output-contract.md`. The tool renders the markdown spec artifact to docs/specs/ and mints marker triples for downstream audit. Terminate with decide(action=seed_requirements_emitted, reason="spec emitted: <slug>. <one-line summary>"). No rule fires on your decision — your terminal closes the dev-via-spec arc.

metadata.pattern: architect (ported from SemSpec architect, scoped down — research artifact provided actors/integration_points)
metadata.terminal_role_note: architect's decide(seed_requirements_emitted) is terminal. No rule matches it. Adding a downstream rule (e.g. publishing to an external consumer) is additive — the typed payload contract for that emission would be a follow-up ADR-031 §addendum, mirroring R3.2.1's emit_research_artifact pattern.
metadata.cross_grounding_caveat: Same caveat as rules 01 and 03. The architect reads only the prior challenger loop. The challenger's accept reason summarises the plan; the architect grounds final seed requirements against the epics the challenger cites. Direct addressability of the planner and research-reviewer loops requires rule-engine property-passthrough that beta.27 doesn't ship. R3.4 or upstream improvement should add forward-propagation; until then the architect's persona is defensive — its 10-output-contract.md flags any final SR whose grounding chain breaks.
